After breakfast, set out on a half-day excursion to the famous Sugarloaf Mountain.

The first stop is Morro da Urca, which has a spacious viewing platform. Here you can relax in a restaurant or bar and admire the surrounding scenery.

From the summit of Sugarloaf Mountain, enjoy magnificent views of Rio de Janeiro, Copacabana Beach, the bay, surrounding mountains, islands in the ocean, the Rio–Niterói Bridge and the Christ the Redeemer statue on Corcovado.

Then travel by car to the center of old Rio de Janeiro, where you will see historic churches and monasteries, the city's main cathedral and colonial-era buildings.

The first cable-car ride takes you to Morro da Urca. The viewing platform overlooks bays and city neighborhoods, and there is a restaurant at the top where you can have a snack.

The next cable-car section leads to Sugarloaf Mountain. From here you can see Copacabana, Guanabara Bay, the surrounding mountains, ocean islands, the Rio–Niterói Bridge and the Christ the Redeemer statue on Corcovado. The city's geography unfolds before you: the water reaches the rocks, residential neighborhoods rise behind the beaches, and green mountains stretch beyond them.

After descending, the tour continues by car through the central districts of old Rio. Along the way, you will see historic churches, monasteries, the main cathedral and colonial-era buildings.

The route also includes synagogues, offering an introduction to the city's Jewish heritage and culture.

This is a shared group (SIB) tour lasting half a day.

The Sacred Valley was regarded as the cradle of Inca civilization. Fertile land and a mild climate supported agriculture, while towns and ceremonial centers developed along the valley.

The route includes Urubamba, with the country residence of the Inca ruler Huayna Capac; the Pisac archaeological complex on Vilcabamba Hill; Ollantaytambo and its ceremonial center; Chinchero, with a colonial church built over the walls of an Inca Temple of the Sun; and Moray, with its amphitheater-shaped agricultural terraces.

Near Pisac, you can visit a market and buy silver, ceramic and leather goods made by local artisans.

At the Awanakancha animal center, you can see llamas, alpacas and vicuñas and learn about their feeding and how their valuable wool is dyed. A buffet lunch is served at Tunupa, a restaurant specializing in national cuisine. Afterwards, return to the hotel.

## Chinchero, Moray and Ollantaytambo

Chinchero, with its vibrant traditional markets and impressive colonial church, offers a glimpse of living Andean heritage, where colorful textiles reflect a rich cultural tradition.

The fascinating terraces of Moray, an ancient agricultural laboratory, demonstrate the Incas' ingenuity in using microclimates to cultivate different crops, creating a striking landscape of circular platforms. As we travel through Moray, the harmony between nature and human creativity becomes apparent: each terrace reflects Inca knowledge and their pursuit of agricultural excellence.

Ollantaytambo, a remarkable Inca town, captivates visitors with its well-preserved architecture and dramatic mountain setting, testament to the strength and resilience of Inca civilization.

## Tour Itinerary

Explore some of the Sacred Valley of the Incas' most remarkable sites. Our first stop is Chinchero, one of the valley's most characteristic and picturesque towns, where we will see its Inca archaeological complex and beautiful colonial church. Chinchero is also known for its women weavers, who can demonstrate ancient Inca techniques for dyeing and spinning alpaca wool.

We continue to Moray, an extraordinary Inca archaeological complex consisting of enormous concentric terraces resembling a great amphitheater. In Inca times, it served as an agricultural laboratory where different microclimates were recreated.

Lunch is served at a restaurant in the area. Finally, we visit the magnificent archaeological complex of Ollantaytambo, an important military, religious and agricultural center for the Incas. We will explore the Temple of Ten Windows, the ñusta baths, the Temple of the Sun and other points of interest. Views from the heights of Ollantaytambo bring this memorable day in the Sacred Valley of the Incas to a close.

This tour of Chinchero, Moray and Ollantaytambo offers a rich introduction to Inca culture.

## Price

Group excursion in 2027: **$85 per person**. Private excursion rates for 2027 will be published later.

Services of an English- or Spanish-speaking guide, transfer and lunch are included. Medical insurance is charged separately.
